mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring specific threshold conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 6.0% for three consecutive months, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 6.0% for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 in any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate robust consumer demand and economic expansion, which together drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through stronger corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS rise, or the interaction effect (measured by the product term) has a Rank IC below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle economic expansions, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening manufacturing activity and potential recession, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of late-cycle expansion periods when INDPRO declines, or the Rank IC for the signal in this regime is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% annually signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which reduces equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises above 2.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly job gains exceed 200,000 (PAYEMS > 200,000), it indicates a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS > 200000, or the Rank IC is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In sustained economic growth regimes, a positive GDP growth surprise (GDPC1 > 2.0% annualized) signals robust demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 > 2.0% in sustained economic growth regimes, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In manufacturing cycles, a simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and GDP growth (GDPC1) signals a supply-side contraction that reduces corporate profitability, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both INDPRO and GDPC1 decline, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.02.
